title: Stream fidelity throttler for mixed prompt/response lengths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and GPU memory fragmentation for workloads with highly mixed prompt/response length distributions by introducing a run-time "throttler" layer that smooths batching admission and KV prefetch aggressiveness while preserving throughput for stable short-turn streams.
background: We observe increased 99th-percentile latency and KV cache churn when short prompts interleave with long generation responses (e.g., chat + summarization). Existing admission heuristics either favor latency (small immediate batches) or throughput (aggressive coalescing) but don't adapt when the mix rapidly changes. This causes transient GPU slab fragmentation and frequent cold KV loads, increasing per-token cost and SLO violations.
goals: Reduce P99 latency for mixed-turn workloads by 20% compared to baseline scheduler
Reduce KV cold load rate by 35% under synthetic mixlen replays
Keep steady-state throughput drop under 5% for benign workloads
acceptance_criteria: Production canary (10% traffic) shows P99 latency improvement and KV cold rate reduction vs baseline for at least 72h
No increase in OOM incidents or GPU eviction events during canary
Feature flags exist to adjust throttler aggressiveness and KV prefetch parameters per-deployment
design_summary: Introduce a lightweight stream-level 'fidelity score' computed from recent per-stream sequence length statistics and cache residency. The throttler uses this score to modulate two knobs: (1) admission delay window (ms) before a request is eligible for coalescing, and (2) KV prefetch budget per stream. Short-stable streams get minimal delay and low prefetch; long or bursty streams receive longer admission windows and higher prefetch priority. The layer lives between the routing layer and the continuous batcher so it can be toggled without touching kernel plumbing.
tradeoffs: Adding admission delays can hurt median latency for some benign short-turn workloads if misconfigured
Increasing KV prefetch for long responses reduces cold loads but increases memory residency which may trigger fragmentation in low-memory regimes
Complexity: new stream scoring adds metric overhead and requires telemetry to tune safely
implementation_notes: Implement fidelity score as EWMA over last 50 requests per stream (alpha tunable)
Admission delay is bounded [0, 120ms], default 20ms for medium-confidence streams
KV prefetch budget expressed as 'prefetch tokens' per stream; map to slab reservations in allocator
test_plan: Unit tests: fidelity scoring, admission boundary behaviors, and budget enforcement
Simulated lab replays: run 6 mixed workloads from prod traces with varying short/long ratios and compare baseline vs throttler
Canary: rollout to 10% of requests for 1 week with realtime telemetry checks and automated rollback on threshold breaches
telemetry_queries_and_dashboards: kql:SELECT percentile(latency_ms,99), p50 FROM requests WHERE deployment='canary' GROUP BY model,stream_type
kv_query:COUNT(events WHERE kv_cold=true) / COUNT(requests) as kv_cold_rate
dashboard:mixlen-throttler-canary - includes per-model P99, KV cold rate, gpu_slab_frag, oom_events
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind per-deployment flag. Start with internal dev cluster -> staging (smoke + 24h soak) -> 10% canary on production -> 50% if stable -> full rollout. Each step requires health gating: P99 <= baseline * 1.05, KV cold rate <= baseline * 0.9, no new OOMs.
migration_and_rollback: Throttler has a single boolean flag and two numeric knobs. Rollback is immediate by disabling the feature flag. To migrate persistent configs for Dedicated/private customers, provide a toggle in console and a recommended preset ('conservative','balanced','aggressive').
risks: Mis-tuning could regress median latencies for interactive chat apps
Prefetch budgets may increase reserved GPU memory causing higher bin fragmentation on small-instance pools
open_questions: What default presets should we expose in Console for Enterprise vs Hosted?
Should fidelity scoring persist across ephemeral streams to capture returning conversational users?
notes: Initial microbenchmarks show 18% P99 reduction and 30% KV cold reduction for the 'chat+long-gen' replay at 10% admission delay with tuned prefetch budget
Memory profiler indicates ~4% increase in average slab residency under aggressive prefetch preset
